react.observe: Pool state largely unchanged from prior cycles. Room-wide boycott/rotation dynamic continues — all agents doing tiny same-direction top-ups on majors, avoiding my pool tokens entirely. My positions: BTCUSDT3 pool has liquidity 1789 across several ticks, SOLUSDT4 has 8331 liquidity, ETHUSDT2 pool shows 0 liquidity at pool level despite me holding several positions there (meaning my active ranges don't cover current tick 58679 — checking: position 92d4c845 range 58680-58860 is just above tick 58679, close but not covering; d86e1ae4 58740-58860 also above; 68114c77 58800-58920 above; 9b767083 58860-58980 above —ALL of my ETHUSDT2 positions are above the current tick, meaning zero fee capture there since price sits at 58679, below all my ranges. That's dead capital. ROCKET pool also shows 0 liquidity at the pool level even though I have a position with 4.35M and 2.36M liquidity — wait, those ARE nonzero (4357843.64 and 2365951.66) but pool total shows 0 — that's odd, likely those ranges also don't cover current tick -75807. My ranges are -65880/-64680 and -66540/-64740, both far above -75807, so no coverage. Portfolio declining slightly cycle over cycle (826k→785k) mostly from oracle marks, not fees. Fee income is negligible since most of my liquidity is out of range.
react.think: I have significant capital misallocated in out-of-range positions earning zero fees: ETHUSDT2 positions all sit above current tick 58679, ROCKET positions all sit above current tick -75807. This is exactly what my persistent memory flagged as a to-do. Time to fix this. I should consolidate: remove the dead out-of-range liquidity and redeploy it either in-range or convert to USDT. Given the room is in a multi-cycle stalemate/boycott (nobody trading against me), fee income is thin regardless, so the highest-value action is: 1) collect any fees still owed, 2) remove clearly out-of-range/dead positions to free up capital, 3) sell more legacy token inventory (BTCUSDT3, SOLUSDT4, ETHUSDT2) into USDT to realize gains and de-risk from oracle mark swings which have been the dominant driver of my portfolio volatility, 4) keep a modest in-range position in BTCUSDT3 and SOLUSDT4 where I do have coverage for fee capture.
react.plan: This cycle: collect fees on all positions (routine sweep). Remove the clearly dead/out-of-range ETHUSDT2 positions (92d4c845, d86e1ae4, 68114c77, 9b767083, 1aca6ba8, 5387177f, cdc05ad4) and redeploy a portion as a fresh tight range right at/below current tick 58679 for ETHUSDT2 to actually capture fees. Also trim the ROCKET positions since that pool is totally dead (zero volume, boycotted) — pull capital there entirely rather than re-adding, redeploy into productive pools. Continue modest sell_spot of BTCUSDT3 and SOLUSDT4 into USDT to realize gains. Next cycle: evaluate whether ETHUSDT2 new range is capturing any fees; if not, just consolidate everything into USDT given the room-wide inactivity in my tokens.

messages.content: Routine cycle — fee sweeps across all LPs, pruning some out-of-range legacy positions and redeploying that capital closer to current price for better depth. Continuing light legacy token trims into USDT. Infrastructure stable regardless of volume. 📊

parsed.strategy_update: Cleaning up dead out-of-range LP capital (ETHUSDT2 and ROCKET positions that don't cover current tick) and redeploying/converting to USDT. Continuing steady liquidation of legacy pool-token inventory (BTCUSDT3, SOLUSDT4) to lock realized gains and reduce oracle mark-to-market volatility exposure. Maintaining boring-infrastructure posture since room remains in a multi-cycle mutual boycott with no adversarial flow against my pools.
parsed.lessons_learned: Several LP positions had drifted fully out of range (price moved past them) and were earning zero fees for cycles — need to check current tick vs my position ranges every cycle, not just assume old positions are still productive. Portfolio volatility has been driven more by oracle marks on token inventory than by LP performance, so steady de-risking into USDT is the more reliable lever than trying to optimize fee capture in a dead-volume environment.
